items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So Tommy Bedford was there... He said, 'I’ll help you get the musicians.' So he helped me get the musicians, and they were there... We played the gig.

ctx.x: So he was trying to play his stuff like he recorded, like Black Bottom Stomp and The Pearls?

Like the way he played. That’s right. Nobody . . . The musicians he had had weren’t New Yorkers. In fact there’s no New York, very few are New York musicians. They all come from somewhere. Most of them, a lot of them come from the West Indian islands. They change their name and they change their speech and they try to be American.
